text: In Tarski's hierarchy of languages L₀ ⊂ L₁ ⊂ L₂ ⊂ ⋯, how is the Liar blocked?
choices: By declaring every self-referential sentence meaningless a priori
By adopting a three-valued logic with truth-value gaps
By treating truth as a single univocal predicate
Each truth predicate Tₙ is typed to apply only to sentences of the lower language Lₙ, so the Liar's fixed-point equation has no solution at any level
explanation: The predicate Tₙ applies only to Lₙ-sentences; a Liar λ ↔ ¬Tₙ(⟨λ⟩) would itself lie in Lₙ₊₁, so Tₙ(⟨λ⟩) is ill-formed and the fixed-point equation is unsolvable at every level. Tarski does not blanket-ban self-reference (option 0), stays classical/two-valued rather than three-valued (option 1 is Kripke's route), and the whole point is that truth is STRATIFIED, not univocal (option 2).
